candidates.lead: It comes after the library was closed earlier this year when staff reported 'bouncy' floors
candidates.evidence_text: Oldham library shut for emergency work as asbestos found in floor - BBC News Image source, Oldham Council Image caption, Asbestos was discovered after 'bouncy' floors triggered an investigation at Royton Library, in Oldham By Ed Barnes Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 1 hour ago A library has been closed for urgent repairs after asbestos and contaminated debris were discovered beneath its floors. Royton Library, in Oldham, closed earlier this year after staff reported sections of flooring had become "bouncy" and inspectors found severe dry rot. Further investigations uncovered asbestos, a hazardous material once widely used in construction, beneath the building's floors the Local Democracy Reporting Service reported . According to a council report, the work is expected to take five to six weeks and is needed to address "immediate health, safety and building risks". Councillors are due to consider the plans on 19 November. Image source, Oldham Council Image caption, It comes after the library was refurbished as part of a £4m scheme which finished in 2024 The total costs of the work is not currently known and any potential costs have not been made public, according to the LDRS. The library will operate from Downey House on Church Street, in Royton, until further notice. Subnum Hariff-Khan, Oldham Council's head of heritage, libraries and arts, said in October: "We know how important Royton Library is to local residents and we're pleased to be able to continue delivering a library service while these essential repairs take place." "We'd like to thank customers for their patience and understanding while these essential works are carried out to secure the future of this important library building." candidates.summary: A decision to suspend a doctor for 12 months has been overruled by a judge on appeal

candidates.practical_angle: Полиция или суд сообщили новое развитие по делу.
candidates.lead: A decision to suspend a doctor for 12 months has been overruled by a judge on appeal
candidates.evidence_text: 'Predatory' Wigan doctor should have been barred, High Court rules - BBC News Image source, Google Image caption, The incidents occurred at the A&E department of the Royal Albert Edward Infirmary, in Wigan, the tribunal heard By Hannah Richardson Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 17 November 2026 A "predatory" doctor should have been struck off for carrying out "sexually motivated examinations" of junior colleagues, a High Court judge has ruled. Dr Khush Bakhat Muhammad Zeeshan was suspended for 12 months by the Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service over incidents at the Royal Albert Infirmary. It took into account that he had not committed the misconduct again, and that some colleagues spoke in his favour. But in overturning the tribunal's decision, Mr Justice Squires said the fact that Zeeshan "had not repeated the misconduct while under active investigation cold not be sufficient" to avoid being barred from the profession. The tribunal found Zeeshan had "exploited the health concerns of two female junior colleagues", touching them on their breasts and bottom, which it said amounted to "serious misconduct". He denied the allegations, which meant he had had "not been able to demonstrate significant insight" into his misconduct, the panel found. It could not "fully assess" the risk that he might do it again, it said. But the panel noted that by the time it was deciding how to punish him, it was five years since the incidents happened. It decided to suspend him for a year "to allow him the opportunity to show that he had developed insight into the concern identified". 'Uphold confidence' The judge said the tribunal had "departed" from its own guidance that said doctors in sexual misconduct cases should generally be struck off. And he said testimonials in his favour were of "limited, if any relevance". He added: "It would not promote confidence in the medical profession to learn that someone who abused his position as a doctor to commit serious sexual misconduct had been allowed to continue to practise [because] they were otherwise a good clinician". The General Medical Council appealed the tribunal's ruling, resulting in the High Court hearing. It said it welcomed the judge's decision, saying it had argued for Zeeshan to be removed from the medical register because of the seriousness of his action and lack of insight. "There is no place for any form of sexual assault, harassment or misconduct in the medical profession. "We will always take action where we believe a sanction may not protect patients or uphold confidence in the profession," it added. Zeeshan's name has now been removed from the register. candidates.lead: Dawud Hussain, 18, is studying to become an electrician but has yet to secure an apprenticeship
candidates.evidence_text: Aspiring electrician applies in vain for 100-plus apprenticeships - BBC News Image caption, Dawud Hussain says he has struggled to find an apprenticeship as an electrician By Haider Saleem , North West and Liv Cleal , Reporting from Altrincham, Greater Manchester Published 17 November 2026 A teenager who wants to become an electrician said he had applied for more than 100 apprenticeships without any success. Dawud Hussain, who is studying electrical installation at Tameside College in Greater Manchester, and also works in a barbershop, said most employers did not even respond to his applications. The 18-year-old spoke to BBC Radio Manchester as a major government-commissioned review set out recommendations for reducing the number of Neets (young people who are not in education, employment or training). City region mayor Bev Craig wants more powers to tackle youth unemployment, including plans for a new apprenticeships hub to double the number available. Dawud, who is seeking an apprenticeship starting in September 2027, said that while his college course was going well, finding an opportunity outside the classroom was proving to be very difficult. "It's like you don't get a chance," he said. "It's tough, it's really tough because when you apply for so much and you don't get a reply back..." He said only a couple of employers had spoken to him, while others either rejected his applications or failed to respond. Dawud said he had been working at a barbershop for about two years but "my first choice is being an electrician". Although he is studying and working, Dawud's difficulties securing an apprenticeship illustrate wider concerns about the number of Neets. Nearly a million young people across the UK are in that position. Image caption, Hairdressing apprentice Honey contacted several salons before securing a place at House of Finesse At the House of Finesse hair salon in Altrincham, Greater Manchester, apprentice Honey said she had contacted five or six salons before securing a place. Most told her they were fully staffed and did not need an apprentice. Salon owner Robert Bennett, whose business employs six apprentices across two salons, said the cost of employing trainees was preventing some businesses from offering opportunities. "There's plenty of apprentices applying because of my industry, but there's just not enough jobs for them," he said. Image caption, Robert Bennett employs six apprentices but says the cost of taking on trainees is putting salons off Greater Manchester mayor Craig said nearly 40,000 young people aged 18 to 24 in the city region were neither earning nor learning. She wants more powers over skills and employment support, including funding for a proposed Greater Manchester Apprenticeships Hub. It would aim to at least double access to apprenticeships and help smaller businesses recruit and train young people. Craig also plans to appoint a new deputy mayor who would serve as Greater Manchester's skills commissioner. She said the region was ready to pilot the approach if ministers granted them the necessary powers and funding. "The system is too broken, it's too fragmented and it's too confusing for our young people," she told BBC Radio Manchester. Dawud called on more employers to offer work experience to help young people build their CVs. "If they don't look at you then what can you really do?" he asked. candidates.lead: Hundreds of customers in Greater Manchester and Lancashire remain without electricity
candidates.evidence_text: Hundreds of properties hit by power cuts after cable incidents - BBC News Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Properties across Greater Manchester and Lancashire are without power By Angela Ferguson North West Published 17 November 2026 Hundreds of properties in Greater Manchester and Lancashire have been hit by power cuts caused by "unexpected" incidents including underground cables. SP Electricity North West (SPENW) said properties in Oldham, Rochdale, Salford, Blackpool, Lancaster, Myerscough and Bilsborrow and North Meols had been affected. SPENW apologised for the disruption, saying that about 279 properties in Myerscough and Bilsborrow in Lancashire had since been reconnected. "Our engineers are working as quickly and safely as possible to restore supplies," said a spokesperson. In Saddleworth, Oldham, 191 properties continue to be affected, with SPENW preparing to send a team out to investigate. In Cadishead and Lower Irlam in Salford, 126 properties are without electricity, with engineers already on site. In the Clifton area of Blackpool, 60 properties are cut off, with engineers en route. In Whalley in the Ribble Valley, 244 properties remain cut off. And in North Meols in West Lancashire, 119 properties are affected, with SPENW preparing to send a crew out. A spokesperson said: "We are aware of separate power cuts affecting properties in parts of Lancashire and Greater Manchester due to faults on the underground electricity network. "Our engineers are working as quickly and safely as possible to restore supplies, and we apologise for the disruption caused." candidates.lead: Conor Rand says Cresta Court Hotel in Altrincham will "end housing asylum seekers" within months
candidates.evidence_text: Altrincham hotel to stop housing asylum seekers, MP says - BBC News Image caption, Cresta Court Hotel in Altrincham has been used to house male asylum seekers since November 2024 By Kevin Fitzpatrick , Greater Manchester political reporter and Rachael Lazaro , North West Published 17 November 2026 A hotel that has been the scene of anti-immigration demonstrations and counter-protests over the last two years will stop housing asylum seekers, the local MP has said. Labour's Conor Rand confirmed the 148-bedroom Cresta Court in Altrincham, Greater Manchester, would "end housing asylum seekers within the next three months as the remaining residents are moved out of the hotel". The local Conservative group claimed the decision came off the back of its "two years of relentless campaigning". A spokesperson for the Home Office said the closure was part of its policy of "closing every asylum hotel and moving asylum seekers into alternative accommodation, including former military sites". Several protests have taken place outside Cresta Court since it began being used to house asylum seekers in 2024, attracting a large police presence. Image source, Reuters Image caption, Anti-immigration protesters gathered outside the hotel in August last year Rand told BBC Radio Manchester : "Hotels are not suitable places to house asylum seekers. "It's bad news for community, bad news for taxpayers, and bad news for people themselves seeking asylum. "It's a practice that should never have been started." Image caption, Labour MP Conor Rand says hotels are "not suitable" places to house asylum seekers In 2023, at the peak of the policy of housing asylum seekers in hotels, 400 were in use at a cost of £9m a day, according to the government. It said "fewer than 160 hotels remain in use today". In August, it was announced three north-west England hotels housing asylum seekers - the Metropole on Blackpool Promenade, Britannia Ashley Hotel in Hale, Altrincham, and Chimney House in Sandbach, Cheshire - had been handed back to their owners. But opposition parties have accused the government of just moving people elsewhere and not fixing the problem. The Home Office spokesperson said: "We are working to fairly house asylum seekers across the country while engaging closely with local authorities to minimise impacts on communities." candidates.lead: Residents who have been informed that their flats will be bulldozed say they will continue to "fight"
candidates.evidence_text: Demolition of Rochdale's Seven Sisters flats devastating, residents say - BBC News Image caption, Christina Hartley and Roy Kitcher say the flats are "home" and they do not want to move By Davinia Ramos , Reporting from in Rochdale and Rebecca Brahde , North West Published 17 November 2026 Residents of a town's tower blocks which are set to be demolished have said it is "devastating" but they will continue to "fight" the decision. Rochdale's Seven Sisters tower blocks, which contain 766 flats, will be replaced by about 600 homes , social landlord Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has said. Demolition of the tower blocks was first proposed in 2017 but was ruled out in 2023 after a local campaign against it, but residents began moving out in October 2025 over long-term safety concerns. Roy Kitcher and Christina Hartley, who have lived in one of the blocks for 14 years, said they were left "upset" and "angry". RBH said demolition was the only "realistic and affordable" option. Kitcher said: "It's devastating news - why they want to knock them down, I don't know." The couple are one of 78 households yet to accept an offer of another home. "This is home and I want to stay here, I don't want to be moving out again," Kitcher added. Hartley said: "I'm just so upset about it and angry." She said the council had asked her to look at accommodation, however it was not in the town. "I want to stay in Rochdale, I'm a Rochdale girl born and bred and I won't move until they find me somewhere round here," she said. Image source, Reuters Image caption, The seven sisters in Rochdale were built in the 1960s A local campaign, previously backed by Rochdale Council, had appealed for the buildings to be refurbished rather than demolished. But previous building surveys have identified structural and electrical issues with the tower blocks, as well as problems with water pumps and roof damage. RBH said refurbishment would have cost at least £269m and would have taken 12 years. Kitcher argued that the flats merely needed the heating and drafty doors and windows "sorting out." "They don't need to be taken back bare brick to be done up like they are saying, they just need to be liveable homes," he said. "I'm still going to fight them, to stop them the best way we can - I've got a meeting with two of the heads of Rochdale Council and I am going to push for them to do something to keep these flats up," he added. Image caption, Joan Wainwright, 72, moved into her flat when she was 36, and bought it ten years later Joan Wainwright who has lived at at Town Mill Brow for 36 years, said: "As far as I'm concerned I am too old. At 72 why should I have to go property hunting. "Thinking about selling all my furniture, which I'm not prepared to do, and starting all over again – no. "The square footage of these flats, as a two bedroom flat is bigger than a lot of terraced housing - so they have got to find us like for like." In a statement, MP for Rochdale Paul Waugh said it was a "sad day for College Bank and for Rochdale. "It's hard to ignore that a lack of investment over many years has contributed to where we are now, and residents have paid the price for that. "What matters now is that residents get certainty and a real say in what comes next," he said, adding that consultation needed to be "genuine" and include residents who had already moved out. "I also want the council and other providers involved in shaping the future of the site, so that it delivers the good-quality homes Rochdale needs," he added. RBH Chief Executive Amanda Newton said: "College Bank has been home to generations of Rochdalians, and we recognise the important place the blocks hold in many people's memories." She said replacing the buildings was the "only realistic and affordable way" to provide suitable homes for residents. "Our top priority is our customers, and our focus remains on supporting every remaining customer to find a home that is right for them," she added. candidates.evidence_text: Large outdoor concerts are due to return to Manchester's Platt Fields Park next summer, with LCD Soundsystem named as the first headliner The American rock band will perform at the park in Fallowfield on 30 July 2027, with Young Fathers, Cowboy Hunters and DJs Erol Alkan and Luka Una also on the bill Organisers said the concert would be part of a series of shows, each with a capacity of 25,000, taking place over two weekends in late July and early August The events, called PlattForm, are being organised by The Warehouse Project, SJM Concerts and Live Nation, with more artists due to be announced in the coming weeks Platt Fields Park previously hosted the Parklife music festival from 2010 to 2012, before it moved to Heaton Park in 2013 to accommodate growing crowds Other music festivals have since taken place at the park, including Flashback Festival in 2022 and 2023

candidates.evidence_text: Large outdoor concerts are due to return to Manchester's Platt Fields Park next summer, with LCD Soundsystem named as the first headliner The American rock band will perform at the park in Fallowfield on 30 July 2027, with Young Fathers, Cowboy Hunters and DJs Erol Alkan and Luka Una also on the bill Organisers said the concert would be part of a series of shows, each with a capacity of 25,000, taking place over two weekends in late July and early August The events, called PlattForm, are being organised by The Warehouse Project, SJM Concerts and Live Nation, with more artists due to be announced in the coming weeks Platt Fields Park previously hosted the Parklife music festival from 2010 to 2012, before it moved to Heaton Park in 2013 to accommodate growing crowds Other music festivals have since taken place at the park, including Flashback Festival in 2022 and 2023

One Manchester expert says they are as prominent as ever - but now A rape expert says the U.K. has “a massive issue with rape myths” following comments made during Russell Brand’s criminal trial Duncan Craig, CEO of We Are Survivors, says he had assumed that some of the comments made by Brand’s defence barrister during his trial “were assigned back into the 1970s and 1980s.” “I genuinely thought that a lot of what he said, I thought those comments were dead. I thought that they were assigned back into the 1970s and 1980s,” says Duncan, on the latest episode of The Mancunian Way podcast “I had absolutely no idea that a barrister would think you were still able to bring those comments into the courtroom. I think it showed, first of all, we have got a massive issue with rape myths that we wrongly thought we’d done a lot of work on as a society “And I also think we’ve got a real moment in time now to say ‘this should never have gone on in the courtroom’

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton The areas in Bolton where £6.5m will be spent fixing potholes after accusations Senior officers told councillors that roads were prioritised according to data and risk with no wards receiving preference Add to preferred sources Comments News Ch Bolton council has said where £6.55m of additional ‘pothole fixing’ funding is to be spent. An extraordinary place scrutiny council meeting heard that the extra cash has been allocated from the Greater Manchester Mayor’s pothole fund to be spend on resurfacing in the borough In a presentation the committee, Dwayne Lowe, a non-political deputy director the council, said the funding would be split in varying amounts across all 20 wards of Bolton . He said where the money would be spent was determined by a ‘data led and risk-based approach’, which selec He added that surveys done by the highways departments pick up condition data including potholes, surface deflection (rutting), cracking and fretting, texture loss, defective iron work and the skid resistance of the road surface He said other considerations included the amount of traffic, bus routes and the vicinity of schools and hospitals and that which wards the roads which needed the work were in was not considered in the process The breakdown by ward showed that £1.366m of the funding would be spent in the Breightmet, the largest amount. The next two highest wards by spend will be Farnworth North with £908,000 allocated and Queens Park and Central with £624,000

candidates.evidence_text: Ashton and Mossley The town that could set the ‘blueprint’ for the rest of Greater Manchester The regeneration of Ashton-under-Lyne could soon be used as a model for the rest of Greater Manchester to follow Add to preferred sources Comments News Georg There’s something going on in Ashton, and it could become a ‘blueprint’ for the rest of Greater Manchester The Tameside town has been chosen to pilot a new way of integrating affordable house building and wider area improvements. Town hall bosses will receive £2.5m from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) to test what is called the ‘Place Based Regeneration Pilot’ The idea behind this pilot is to bring work to build new homes; retrofit current housing; and environmental improvements under one roof It is hoped that this collaborative approach between public bodies could help speed up development and reduce costs compared to projects being brought forward individually. If successful, the same methods could be used in regeneration projects across the city-region Deputy mayor for Greater Manchester, Paul Dennett, told the latest GMCA meeting: “This will set a blueprint for how we do regeneration across the region.”

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport ASDA pulls out of controversial plan which attracted 'most objections in Stockport history' “We look forward to seeing the store delivered in due course, providing more shopping choices for local people" Add to preferred sources Comments New Supermarket chain ASDA has confirmed they have pulled out of a controversial project in Stockport after it was given the green light by planners Earlier this year, Stockport council rejected plans to demolish a car repair garage and MOT test centre and replace it with a new shop at 22 Marple Road in Offerton. The plans made reference to the new unit being occupied by ASDA Express, but were developer-led The plans came up against significant opposition from people in the area with a letter of objection signed by 1,800 people and 1,272 individual comments submitted on Stockport council’s planning portal. The biggest concern was the new shop’s impact on local independent businesses Town hall bosses later rejected the plans arguing the plans did not show ‘the proposed retail use could be properly and safely serviced without causing a detrimental impact on highway safety and parking’. 13 car parking spaces are included in the plans However Aim Capital Ltd appealed the local authority’s decision. Earlier this week, planning inspector Katie McDonald overruled Stockport council and gave the greenlight for the development to go ahead

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre Cyclist, 19, killed in Manchester city centre after 'unaware' truck driver crashed into him - trial Michael Yates, 55, denies causing death by careless driving off Deansgate, in Manchester Add to preferred sources News Greta Sim A man accused of causing death by careless driving in Manchester city centre 'was not aware' he had struck a teenage cyclist until after the collision, and had to be notified by members of the public, a trial has heard Nawaf Al-Ghamdi, 19, had been cycling along Great Bridgewater Street in Manchester city centre on May 24, 2023, when he collided with a flatbed truck. He was killed in the incident, jurors in a trial at Manchester Crown Court were told yesterday (November 17) The driver of the truck, Michael Yates, 58, of Kirkfell Walk in Oldham , denies causing Mr Al-Ghamdi's death. Prosecutor Niamh McGinty told jurors in her opening of the case that the collision took place just before mid-day Mr Yates had been driving a flat-bed truck eastwards after turning left off Deansgate , and was delivering some equipment to a building site. Mr Al-Ghamdi was travelling along the same road behind Mr Yates, Ms McGinty said, riding a bike in the cycle lane to the left of the truck Upon approaching the junction with Watson Street, where the lights were red, Mr Yates slowed down, while Mr Al-Ghamdi continued in the cycle lane towards the rear of the vehicle

New knife disposal bins were placed in Tyldesley and Ashton in October in a bid to safely get rid of potential weapons which could lead to ha The bin in Tyldesley, which can be found just outside The Square, has had more than 110 knives deposited, with more than 60 surrendered in the bin in Ashton which is located in The Gerard Centre A Wigan council spokesperson said: “These new bins add to the existing eight across Wigan borough. Through the knife bins and safer knife exchange initiatives, 7,961 weapons and bladed articles have been removed from circulation “Each disposal has been deposited over a year-long period and represents a commitment from everyone across the borough to reduce knife harm.” In July, 2025, the council voted to adopt and support the Let’s Be Blunt campaign, which aspires to reduce knife crime through practical, everyday actions

This marked the 40th arrest under Operation Sherwood The multi-agency operation was launched in 2022, following the publication of a 'review into historic safeguarding practices in the borough of Oldham’. The review, published almost three years after being commissioned, found that children in Oldham were being exploited and let do The probe is focused on reports of child sexual exploitation and abuse between 2010 and 2014. GMP said the arrest came yesterday as 'efforts were ramped up' and 'new evidence was uncovered' Two other men were also arrested earlier this month. On November 12, a 44-year-old man was arrested in Oldham on suspicion of rape. A 40-year-old man was also arrested in Bolton on suspicion of rape. Both men have been bailed pending further enquiries

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton The areas in Bolton where £6.5m will be spent fixing potholes after accusations Senior officers told councillors that roads were prioritised according to data and risk with no wards receiving preference Add to preferred sources Comments News Ch Bolton council has said where £6.55m of additional ‘pothole fixing’ funding is to be spent. An extraordinary place scrutiny council meeting heard that the extra cash has been allocated from the Greater Manchester Mayor’s pothole fund to be spend on resurfacing in the borough In a presentation the committee, Dwayne Lowe, a non-political deputy director the council, said the funding would be split in varying amounts across all 20 wards of Bolton . He said where the money would be spent was determined by a ‘data led and risk-based approach’, which selec He added that surveys done by the highways departments pick up condition data including potholes, surface deflection (rutting), cracking and fretting, texture loss, defective iron work and the skid resistance of the road surface He said other considerations included the amount of traffic, bus routes and the vicinity of schools and hospitals and that which wards the roads which needed the work were in was not considered in the process The breakdown by ward showed that £1.366m of the funding would be spent in the Breightmet, the largest amount. The next two highest wards by spend will be Farnworth North with £908,000 allocated and Queens Park and Central with £624,000

Town hall bosses will receive £2.5m from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) to test what is called the ‘Place Based Regeneration Pilot’ The idea behind this pilot is to bring work to build new homes; retrofit current housing; and environmental improvements under one roof It is hoped that this collaborative approach between public bodies could help speed up development and reduce costs compared to projects being brought forward individually. candidates.evidence_text: Stockport ASDA pulls out of controversial plan which attracted 'most objections in Stockport history' “We look forward to seeing the store delivered in due course, providing more shopping choices for local people" Add to preferred sources Comments New Supermarket chain ASDA has confirmed they have pulled out of a controversial project in Stockport after it was given the green light by planners Earlier this year, Stockport council rejected plans to demolish a car repair garage and MOT test centre and replace it with a new shop at 22 Marple Road in Offerton. The plans made reference to the new unit being occupied by ASDA Express, but were developer-led The plans came up against significant opposition from people in the area with a letter of objection signed by 1,800 people and 1,272 individual comments submitted on Stockport council’s planning portal. The biggest concern was the new shop’s impact on local independent businesses Town hall bosses later rejected the plans arguing the plans did not show ‘the proposed retail use could be properly and safely serviced without causing a detrimental impact on highway safety and parking’. 13 car parking spaces are included in the plans However Aim Capital Ltd appealed the local authority’s decision. Earlier this week, planning inspector Katie McDonald overruled Stockport council and gave the greenlight for the development to go ahead

candidates.evidence_text: Courts The 'accident waiting to happen' that cost a devoted dad, 42, his life John Graveson was killed instantly at his work in Tameside John Graveson died in March 2023 (Image: Family handout) Add to preferred sources News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 05:51, 18 Nov 2026 When John Graveson waved goodbye to his family three years ago, he had every reason to believe he would return home that evening The 42-year-old went to work on the morning of March 3, 2023, as he had done countless times before, expecting to come home to his partner Shelly and their daughter. His daughter continues to grow, reaching milestones without her dad by her side And now, a jury has found that the circumstances which led to Mr Graveson's death were entirely preventable, finding the waste management company he worked for guilty of corporate manslaughter Mr Graveson was employed as a picker at AMP NW Ltd - now Waste Solutions Mcr Ltd - at Aspire House industrial estate in Dukinfield, Tameside

New knife disposal bins were placed in Tyldesley and Ashton in October in a bid to safely get rid of potential weapons which could lead to ha The bin in Tyldesley, which can be found just outside The Square, has had more than 110 knives deposited, with more than 60 surrendered in the bin in Ashton which is located in The Gerard Centre A Wigan council spokesperson said: “These new bins add to the existing eight across Wigan borough. Through the knife bins and safer knife exchange initiatives, 7,961 weapons and bladed articles have been removed from circulation “Each disposal has been deposited over a year-long period and represents a commitment from everyone across the borough to reduce knife harm.” In July, 2025, the council voted to adopt and support the Let’s Be Blunt campaign, which aspires to reduce knife crime through practical, everyday actions

It was reported that two men dressed in all black and wearing face coverings were seen leaving the premises with the festive foliage - which is understood to have been According to the force, Bolton Response Team were called and located the suspects shortly afterwards at a nearby address. Two males, aged 37 and 49, have been arrested on suspicion of shoplifting Sergeant Bella Mercer from the GMP Bolton response team said: "Christmas should be the time for giving, not stealing. Our officers moved quickly to secure two arrests and ensured Christmas spirit was alive in Bolton by returning the tree to the business "Your reports are so important to our response to criminality in your area. I'd like to thank those who reported this incident to us today, and all those who continue to raise their concerns of incidents in the area "You all support our mission to reducing crime in Bolton and our officers will continue to work early mornings, late nights, and all through the dark winter period to ensure you all have a safe Christmas.”

The 27-year-old, from Liverpool, targeted petrol stations in Warrington, Davenham, Rudheath, Winsford and Crewe between August and September 20 His downfall came on September 24 when he targeted the Texaco Garage on King Street in Rudheath. The incident was reported to police who were deployed to the scene Lawrence was arrested nearby and during a search of his van, officers found 10 false number plates. An investigation was launched and police were able to link Lawrence to ten thefts of fuel across Cheshire, with a total value of £2661.37 Lawrence, of Feltwood Walk, Liverpool, appeared at Chester Crown Court last Friday (November 13). He had earlier pleaded guilty to ten counts of theft of fuel, two counts of attempted theft of fuel, going equipped for theft, fraudulent use of a registration mark, driving without

candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 14 October 2026 at 10:33am Kirith Entwistle, the Labour MP for Bolton North East, has said she found the current court system "triggering" and had to watch her abuser "stare at her". Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

candidates.evidence_text: A Company been found guilty of corporate manslaughter at Manchester Crown Court and Section 2 Health & Safety at Work Act offence after the death of an employee at skip hire yard in Dukinfield Anthony Elston aged 49 , Clifton – owner of AMP NW Ltd, has been found guilty of Section 2 Health & Safety at Work Act offence and John Horan aged Burnley, has been found guilty of Section 7 – Health & Safety at Work Act The court heard that on the morning of 3 March 2023, John Horan, a yard manager and machine operator employed by AMP NW Ltd, was operating a Hyundai HW140 excavator within the yard At the same time, 42-year-old John Graveson, who had worked at the site as a waste picker for approximately one year, was walking through the yard. John Graveson moved alongside the excavator before continuing behind it As John Graveson passed behind the excavator, Horan placed the vehicle into reverse and began manoeuvring backwards. Although the excavator’s reversing alarm was sounding and its blue warning lights were illuminated, Horan remained facing forwards and failed to observe John Grave The excavator struck John Graveson, and proceeded to crush him, causing catastrophic injuries from which he sadly died at the scene

evidence_packet.evidence_text: From bringing lost pieces of Salford’s industrial past back to life through virtual reality to turning microscopic organisms from the River Irwell into sound and light, MediaCity is preparing to showcase creativity in all its forms at BEYOND Festival Taking place on Monday 23 November, the free festival will open up MediaCity’s spaces to an evening of immersive experiences, experimental art, live music and creative discovery, bringing together some of Greater Manchester’s most exciting artists, researchers and innovators Alice Webb, CEO of MediaCity said “MediaCity is where bold ideas come to life and this is exactly what BEYOND Festival is about. We’re bringing together artists, researchers and creative talent who are exploring what’s possible when technology, culture and creativity collide. Fro Paul Dennett, City Mayor of Salford said “BEYOND Festival reflects the creativity, ambition and collaboration that make Salford such a special place to live, work and create. By bringing together artists, researchers, businesses and communities, it creates opportunities to explor Visitors will get the opportunity to experience the first public showing of Nested Cinema, an AHRC-funded research project at the University of Salford that reimagines film by orchestrating technology in layers around it. The installation features Sisyphos, a triptych film by Kay Highlights will also include a digital showcase of artists who have taken part in the CreaTech Artist CoLab Artist Development Programme , a city-wide initiative supporting Salford-based artists to explore emerging technologies through mentoring, collaboration and experimentation

candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police (GMP) took control of about 400 automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras that were supposed to be used to enforce the planned region-wide low-emission zone And they have been used to make "multiple arrests", a senior officer said The cameras were installed as part of Greater Manchester's drive to cut the number of high-emission vehicles on the regions roads, but the plans were dropped in favour of other efforts to make the region's transport network more environmentally friendly Deputy chief constable Terry Woods told Greater Manchester's police, fire and crime panel on Monday the system was making a significant difference "It's been tangible, multiple arrests on the back of that system and it's keeping people safe," he said Deputy Mayor Kate Green said: "They are not speed cameras, they are being used for crime detection and as an investigative tool."

candidates.title: Construction Begins on Two New Game-Changing Sports Hubs for Wythenshawe Communities
candidates.summary: Construction has begun at two major new Football Foundation multisport Hubs in Wythenshawe, marking a significant milestone in the transformation of community sport across South Manchester

candidates.evidence_text: Construction Begins on Two New Game-Changing Sports Hubs for Wythenshawe Communities | Manchester City Council Construction Begins on Two New Game-Changing Sports Hubs for Wythenshawe Communities Tuesday 17 November 2026 Construction has begun at two major new Football Foundation multisport Hubs in Wythenshawe, marking a significant milestone in the transformation of community sport across South Manchester. The two new sites will help transform grassroots sport, improve health and wellbeing, and create new opportunities for thousands of local people. Backed by £11 million of investment from the Premier League, The FA and Government's Football Foundation, alongside Manchester City Council, the NHS and other local authority partners, the development at Wythenshawe Park and Wythenshawe Sports Ground will provide modern, inclusive and accessible facilities that support people of all ages and abilities to get active, connect with their communities and enjoy sport year-round. As construction got underway, partners celebrated the milestone with a special ‘spade-in-the-ground' event on 12 November 2026. The event was attended by representatives of all three Football Foundation partners: the Premier League, The FA and Government, as well as representatives of the Manchester County FA, the Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig OBE, and local MP, Mike Kane. Wythenshawe Sports Ground Hub is a flagship women's and girls' site and will be the central venue for the South Manchester Girls' League once built. Wythenshawe Park Hub, meanwhile, will include a dedicated GP surgery, which will support an integrated approach to health and wellbeing in the community. Facilities across the two Hubs will include six full-size floodlit 3G pitches, multi-use sports areas for recreational use, improved grass pitches, new community buildings which will house the GP surgery, changing pavilions, improved parking and cafés and meeting spaces. Together, the two projects represent an investment of more than £22 million into grassroots sports infrastructure and will create high-quality facilities capable of serving thousands of local residents for generations to come. A New Home for Community Sport Identified in the Local Football Facility Plan for Manchester, the Hubs will create significantly more opportunities for the local community to come together through sport. Local Football Facility Plans were created by the Football Foundation in partnership with local authorities, County FAs and other community stakeholders. Collectively, these Local Plans act as a blueprint for providing the grassroots football facility improvements that each community across the country needs and deserves Both projects will also help tackle barriers to participation, creating welcoming spaces where people can come together to play sport, regardless of their background. The developments will support a wide range of activities, including youth engagement, women's and girls' football, disability sport and walking football, as well as providing community health services. Following the event, Robert Sullivan, CEO at the Football Foundation, said: "The new Hubs at Wythenshawe Park and Wythenshawe Sports Ground are about far more than pitches. Thanks to the support of our funding partners, the Premier League, The FA and Government, the Football Foundation is creating more opportunities for people to be active, improve physical and mental wellbeing and build stronger community connections. "The start of construction marks the beginning of an exciting new chapter for Wythenshawe, with the Hubs set to deliver lasting benefits for local communities and inspire more people to get involved in sport. "By working in partnership with local authorities, our multisport Hub sites make sure facilities are tailored to the needs of local clubs and organisations, allowing them to thrive and ensuring that more across the community have access to a great place to play." Councillor Shazia Butt, Executive Member for Culture, Leisure and Libraries, Manchester City Council said: “This investment is about much more than new buildings. It is about creating a connected neighbourhood hub where sport, health, education and community services come together to help people live healthier, more active lives. candidates.lead: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund
candidates.evidence_text: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund The funding forms part of an £18million government programme to create or refurbish playgrounds in England's areas of greatest need over the next two years The government selected Failsworth to receive a share of the fund, with three play areas identified as eligible for investment through the programme for 66 local authorities Funding will be used to improve playground facilities and support community-led design and engagement activities, giving residents the opportunity to help shape the future of these spaces The three eligible sites are Higher Memorial Park which will receive £160,000, Daisy Nook Country Park which will receive £60,000 and Lower Memorial Park which has been allocated £50,000 A larger share will go to Higher Memorial Park because this has received significantly less external investment than the other locations in recent years

candidates.lead: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026
candidates.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026 The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications Residents will be asked the following question “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area

candidates.evidence_text: Press release — 17 November 2026 10:16 Share Share this story Copy link Link copied! Download Hundreds of Bury residents are set to benefit from practical support this winter through Bury Council's Winter Well programme Led by Bury Council's Public Health team and delivered in partnership with local organisations, the programme aims to help residents stay healthy, warm and connected during the colder months. It provides advice and support on cost-of-living pressures, heating and fuel costs, food As part of the programme, 500 Winter Well packs are being distributed to older and more vulnerable residents across the borough. The packs contain practical items including thermal socks, blankets, gloves, hand warmers, wind-up torches, Independent Age Winterwise booklets and inf To ensure the packs reach those most in need, they have been distributed through a range of community groups and services across Bury The initiative has been delivered through collaboration between Public Health, Adult Social Care, Bury Housing and Homelessness Teams, Age UK Bury, Persona, the Staying Well Team, VCFA, Bury Older People's Network (BOPN), the Health Protection Team and the Climate Action Team

candidates.evidence_text: Leigh Sports Village hosted the Believe in Business Festival this year Employers and entrepreneurs came together to celebrate the strength and innovation of the borough’s business community at the return of this year’s Believe in Business Festival Firmly established as one of the borough's flagship business events, the Believe in Business Festival was held at Leigh Sports Village for the first time on Thursday 12th November, with practical support from local, regional, and national organisations Attendees had access to a packed programme of workshops, panel discussions and expert advice sessions covering a range of topics affecting modern businesses, including business growth, artificial intelligence, digital marketing, workforce development, social value, and more Councillor Dane Anderton, cabinet portfolio holder for economic development and regeneration said: "The Believe in Business Festival continues to demonstrate the talent, innovation, and entrepreneurial spirit that exists across Wigan Borough “Our business community plays a crucial role in creating jobs, attracting investment and supporting local residents, and it was fantastic to see the event hosted in Leigh with so many businesses and partners represented once again."

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.lead: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre […] The post Sona Jobarteh Tour appeared first on Band on the Wall
candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

candidates.lead: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians.
candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Counter Manchester , the much-anticipated new restaurant from Open Restaurant Group , opens its doors today at 12pm. It is the group’s first opening in Manchester city centre and brings a theatrical approach to dining to the heart of the city Led by acclaimed chef Andrew Sheridan, Counter is located in Manchester’s Island Building on John Dalton Street and has 60 covers. It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, so the atmosphere and experienc Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

Cadno Lounge, Neath . Loungers, the West Country‑based café‑bar group, will open Fosforo Lounge, King Street in Stretford on Saturday 28th November 2026, creating around 30 new jobs for local people.. . Fosforo Lounge will be open all day, every day, serving breakfast, brunch, lunch, dinner and drinks, with dedicated kids’, gluten‑free and vegan menus. . The site on King Street has been transformed by the Loungers design team into a warm, eclectic ‘home from home’ – their signature style. Fosforo translates to matchstick and is a nod to Manchester-based painter LS Lowry’s ‘matchstick men’ style.. . Fosforo Lounge’s all‑day menu will cater for every taste, from hearty comfort food to healthier choices and indulgent treats. Families are a major focus, with games, books, colouring materials, high chairs and baby‑changing facilities available for Little Loungers.. . With community at its heart, Fosforo Lounge will offer a welcoming space for regular meet‑ups, business catch‑ups, book clubs, knitting groups, parent‑and‑baby sessions, creative workshops and more. Local groups looking for a friendly, flexible venue will be encouraged to get in touch.. . Vix Connolly, General Manager, Fosforo Lounge said: “We’re so looking forward to welcoming everyone to Fosforo Lounge on the 28th November. Becoming a genuine part of the community is incredibly important to us, and we can’t wait to meet our neighbours and get involved locally.. . “If you’re looking for a friendly, flexible space for events or group meet‑ups, pop in once we’re open – we’d love to chat and see how we can help.”. . . . . . . candidates.evidence_text: The £35 million project set within 154 acres has transformed the former site of Worsley New Hall, restoring the historic walled garden, lake and surviving buildings Originally built for the 1st Earl of Ellesmere between 1840 and 1845, Worsley New Hall was a grand Gothic-style mansion, complete with glorious, formal landscaped gardens It’s now one of UK’s must-see gardens with so much to enjoy for visitors of all ages Step inside the magnificent 11-acre Weston Walled Garden, the site’s jewel in the crown. We're launching The Inside Track , a new monthly online session designed to help Manchester Digital members stay informed, discover new opportunities and make the most of their membership Whether you've recently joined Manchester Digital or have been part of our community for years, The Inside Track is your chance to catch up with our team, find out what's happening across the network and explore ways to get more involved Taking place on the last Wednesday of each month, these free, members-only sessions will bring you up to speed on the latest developments, events and opportunities across Manchester Digital, all in just 30 minutes Each session will feature a topical focus, alongside practical updates on upcoming events, programmes, speaking opportunities and ways to raise your business's profile There'll also be time to ask questions, share your priorities and find out how we can help you get more value from your membership Our first edition at midday on 25th November will focus on some of the biggest opportunities coming up across the Manchester Digital community

candidates.evidence_text: POWWR strengthens team with double appointment | Bdaily Joe Hemmings, left, and Ryan Ansell, who have joined POWWR POWWR strengthens team with double appointment Manchester-based energy software provider POWWR has strengthened its business development team with two appointments as it continues to expand. Ryan Ansell and Joe Hemmings join as SME business development managers, supporting the company’s growing network of energy brokers. Ryan brings 14 years’ experience in the energy industry, having previously held account management and relationship management roles at Online Direct. In his new position, he will focus on strengthening existing broker partnerships and developing new relationships to support business growth. Ryan said: “POWWR’s positive culture throughout the business really stood out to me. “All members of staff have been very welcoming and supportive. “I am excited to join the team at such a pivotal time and looking forward to leveraging my experience to help drive growth and add value to POWWR’s existing clients.” Joe also joins from Online Direct, where he spent four years as an account manager, having previously worked in the metering team at Opus. His role will involve working directly with brokers, building relationships and gathering feedback to support POWWR’s product development. Joe added: “I’m really excited and honoured to join POWWR at such a great time for the business. “Although I mainly work remotely, the company does a great job at keeping everyone well connected. “I have enjoyed my time out on the road, introducing myself to brokers, meeting them face-to-face and developing deeper relationships.” Their appointments follow a period of growth for the company, which has increased its headcount by 20 per cent since Paul Hodnett became chief executive earlier this year, following investment from Five Elms Capital. Paul added: “We are thrilled to welcome Ansell and Hemmings to our growing team. “What makes POWWR such a force in the industry is the people we have working for us. “I have no doubt that Ansell and Hemmings will help the brokers we work with win more deals and grow their businesses.” Want your business, product or service to be seen regionally and nationally? candidates.evidence_text: Legal AI leader Clio expands global footprint in Salford - Invest Manchester Skip to main content Skip to footer Opens in a new tab Digital, cyber & AI , Financial, professional, business services Legal AI leader Clio expands global footprint in Salford Published on November 11, 2026 News Clio , the global leader in legal AI, expands its UK presence with a move to Eden , having signed a deal with ECF to take the first fitted and furnished suite in Manchester’s highly sustainable, 12-storey workplace in New Bailey . Moving from Alderley Edge, Clio’s new 5,134 sq. ft office is a turnkey space designed for high-growth businesses, with 50 fixed workstations, dedicated pods and booths for focused work, board and meeting rooms, a kitchen complete with a dining area, and flexible touchdown spaces built to support collaboration. Already home to law firm TLT, accountancy and business advisory firm BDO, and the PE-backed professional services group Leonard Curtis, Eden offers move-in-ready office space designed to make taking on a new workspace simpler and more straightforward. Delivered by ECF, our partnership with Homes England’s National Housing Bank, L&G and Muse , the turnkey model streamlined Clio’s move into its new space, reducing the time and complexity typically associated with a traditional office fit-out. Moving into a city centre location brings Clio closer to its growing UK customer base following its recent acquisition of Manchester-based ShareDo, now Clio Operate , the legal work management platform for large firms and enterprise legal teams. Eden’s central location and modern amenities also support Clio’s continued growth by strengthening its ability to attract and retain talent. Following the successful letting of its first fitted and furnished workspace, ECF is now underway with two additional suites within Eden, delivered to a similar specification. The first of the two new suites will be available from December 2026, with the second scheduled to be available from early 2027. This will include a 4,886 sq. ft office on the same floor as Clio, and a 10,000 sq ft. space on the second floor, with ECF responding to continued demand for turnkey solutions of this nature across the sector. Organisations that move to Eden send a clear message that they’re committed to fostering a healthy, connected and collaborative workforce centred around wellness and wellbeing, along with demonstrating their ambition to create a sustainable future. Eden itself is home to a range of amenities, including on-site café, Spice & Grind, a yoga/contemplation studio, and a roof terrace, each designed to offer occupants space to take a break from day-to-day work schedules. Elsewhere there are enhanced fresh air rates which boost cognitive function; there’s an emphasis on natural light and planting to provide a connection to nature; and the whole building embraces the WELL Building Standard Principles to create a workplace that supports productivity and collaboration. In-keeping with Eden’s green credentials – which include being net zero carbon in operation – the new fitted and furnished suite has been designed with sustainability at its heart too, enabling the space to become the first fit-out in the UK to achieve both SKA V2 Gold certification and a Net Zero Aligned approach. This is in part thanks to a range of specific fixtures and furnishings which have been prioritised to incorporate high levels of circularity. This includes the use of cork for its renewable and recyclable properties, utilisation of 100% of the CAT A lighting, and the specification of recycled denim for elements of the kitchen chairs. Eden’s sustainability credentials and its focus on employee wellbeing were significant factors in Clio’s decision. Laura Percy, development director, said : “Welcoming Clio to Eden’s first fitted and furnished suite represents another significant staging post in this remarkable building’s journey, and we’re delighted to support Clio’s growth as it takes this next step. “Being part of Eden offers a working experience unlike any other, with a strong focus on connectivity, collaboration, wellbeing and sustainability. It is the ideal place for businesses looking to build a brighter future for both the company and its team. “Since its completion in 2024 Eden has become a Manchester landmark, with a green wall façade adorned with 350,000 plants. candidates.evidence_text: BBC Casualty star Anna Chell will take to the stage at Manchester theatre 53two this Christmas as part of the cast of A Trifle And A Turkey Crown , alongside actor and 53two Creative Director Simon Naylor The premiere, written by Rebekah Harrison, who is no stranger to The Arches, runs from Wed 16 Dec – Wed 23 Dec. It tells the story of four people, living in a Northern town, whose lives begin to intertwine as Christmas approaches “ A Trifle And A Turkey Crown offers audiences something different: a contemporary Christmas story centred on ordinary lives, unexpected relationships and the connections that can form between people who have been living only metres apart.” For Chell, the production also represents something of a return home. Before establishing herself on screen, Anna trained with Manchester Actors Platform, the actor-training and development organisation that would later evolve into 53two She went on to build a successful career across stage and screen and is now best known to television audiences as Jodie Whyte in BBC’s long-running medical drama Casualty , a role she first took on in 2023 and in which she has since become a series regular Now, many years after training with Manchester Actors Platform, she returns to the organisation’s home as part of 53two’s Christmas production

Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.evidence_text: The Bridgewater Hall , City Centre 19 November 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit In 1996, Thomas Adès wrote a work celebrating the opening of The Bridgewater Hall – a four-minute showpiece, These Premises Are Alarmed , that the Observer called “packed with detailed, fascinating invention.” But for all its “utmost, fine-grained, virtuosity,” it doesn’t take it Adès also conducts his own Asyla , the piece that made his name in the years just after. The title is the Latin plural of “asylum”, which can mean both a place of refuge and an institution for the insane – and the piece plays on this plurality. Its third movement, Ecstasio , is s Between these two pieces comes a world premiere: Gabriella Smith’s How To Be A Bird , written for tonight’s soloist Pekka Kuusisto. Hailed by the LA Times as “an outright sensation”, Smith writes music drawn from field recordings and underwater microphones, looking for what she c The evening closes with Stravinsky’s Firebird Suite , one of the happiest accidents in musical history. Sergei Diaghilev, head of the Ballets Russes, saw his first three choices to score a new ballet fall through before he gambled on an unproven 27-year-old; Stravinsky himself la Four works, then, that each began as a risk on someone (to varying degrees) untested – Stravinsky in 1910, Adès in 1996, Smith tonight. If this is Adès’s opening statement as Principal Guest Conductor, it’s a heartening one: a little faith in emerging composers can go a long way

A Champions League winner, a Premier League winner and an FA Cup winner after an incredible season with Manchester City Now the England international is at a significant crossroads. He's missed the last four matches with loan club Everton owing to a disciplinary breach and while he could return to action this weekend against Brentford his long-term future is uncertain The arrival of Enzo Maresca at the Etihad in the summer, someone with whom Grealish forged a close bond during the 2022-23 season when the Italian was on Pep Guardiola's coaching staff, was viewed by some as a potential olive branch for the 31-year-old Get all the best Man City news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the MEN!
